segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: These -go verbs, these verbs that take -go instead of -o for the I-version in the present,

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: also behave a little bit strangely in the future tenses, in the will and would tenses.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So we can look at that now, and whilst looking at it, revise the endings that we learnt for will and would.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So we said that our will endings, what we add on to the to-form of the verb to get will, are the same as those very irregular versions of haber in the present. So we can make that connection to help us internalise them.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Can you talk me through those will endings?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: So it's -é for I, and -emos for us...

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: For we, very good.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: -á for he, she, it, and you formal, -án for they...

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: They or you plural, and the last one, you informal?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: -ás.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. So we have the endings.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: And our endings for would, which again we are adding on to the to-form of the verb,

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: we need to remember one key sound for would.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: If we remember how to say I would like, that's a nice hook to remember the key sound. So what is the key sound?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: -ía.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: -ía. And then onto -ía we can add on, of course, our -mos or -n or -s if we need to. Good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So -go verbs, these verbs that have -go and then -ga for the mood tense,

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: when they are building the futures, they have a contraction,

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: but they all make the same contraction. For example,

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: I will have is tendré. Tendré.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Tendré.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Tendré. So of course, it should be teneré, no? But it's tendré.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So that last e of tener turns into a d, and we get tendré.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: This is a contraction because it means we end up with two syllables instead of three. It would be teneré, but it's tendré, which just makes everything a little bit more efficient.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: But all of these verbs, these -go verbs, are behaving in a similar way. So we have to come...

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Venir.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Venir. And I will come?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Vendré.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Vendré, very good. I would come? The same contraction for both futures.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Vendría.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Vendría, good. I would come. We would come?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Vendríamos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Vendríamos. We would come later, but we don't have time. We would come later, but we don't have time.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Vendríamos más tarde, pero no tenemos tiempo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good! Vendríamos más tarde, pero no tenemos tiempo. What was to put?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Poner.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: And I put?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Pongo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Pongo. So this -go alerts us to the fact that this verb will behave in this irregular way as well. So if you want to say, I will put it here, how will it be? I will put it here.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Lo pondré aquí.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Lo pondré aquí. I would put it here. I would put it here?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Lo pondría aquí.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. We would put it here?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Lo pondríamos aquí.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Lo pondríamos aquí. And we will put it here?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Lo pondremos aquí.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Lo pondremos aquí. What was to leave or to go out?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Salir.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Salir. I leave or I go out?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Salgo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Salgo. So again this -go can set off our little alarm bell that this verb will probably be irregular in the futures. So how would you say, I would leave or I would go out?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Saldría.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Saldría, good. You would leave or you would go out, informally?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Saldrías.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Saldrías. Will you leave, will you go out tonight? Will you go out tonight?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: ¿Saldrías esta noche?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: That's would you. Now we want will you.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: ¿Saldrás esta noche?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. ¿Saldrás esta noche? But of course we have esta noche, which is future context, so we could just use the present. We could just say, you go out tonight? We don't need the future. So how would that be?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: ¿Sales esta noche?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: ¿Sales esta noche? Good. So for most -go verbs, we take off the -go and we put -dré for I will, and -dría for I would.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: With most of them. Traer, to bring, doesn't do it: traeré, I will bring; atraeré, I will attract; distraeré, I will distract. But most of these that have -go will go to -dría or -dré.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Hacer and decir, to do or to make, or to say or to tell, hacer and decir, are particularly irregular, and we've already seen this.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: We've seen how after haber they become hecho and dicho. It's very irregular.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: We saw how the informal command from hacer is haz, h-a-z, again irregular. And here as well.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: I will do is haré. So it's not following this rule. It's even more irregular. We have haré. Haré: I will do or I will make.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Haré.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: H-a-r-é, haré. And all we need to do is identify one of these irregularities, and then we understand that all of will and all of would will use this same base, the same base that haré has used. Huh? So we will do or we will make is...

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Haremos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. And we would do or we would make?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Haríamos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Haríamos. We would do it, but we're busy now. We would do it, but we're busy now.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Lo haríamos, pero estamos...

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Occupied?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: ...ocupados ahora.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good! Lo haríamos, pero estamos ocupados ahora. We would do it, but we're busy now. So haríamos is we would do or we would make. And what is we will do or we will make?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Haremos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Haremos. And they will do, they will make?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Harán.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Harán. I would say or I would tell is diría. So we get from decir, diría. I would say, he would say, she would say, you formal would say...

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Diría.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So, like I said, we just need one of these versions to understand how the rest would be. So if diría is I would say or I would tell, how is I will say or I will tell?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Diré.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Diré. I will tell you later, speaking informally.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Te diré más tarde.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good! Te diré más tarde. And of course having future context with más tarde, we could just say...

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Te digo más tarde.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good! Te digo más tarde. I tell you later. What was to be able to?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Poder.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Poder. How do you say I would be able to, or I could?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Podría.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Podría, good. The e falls out. So this is a different irregularity. This is not a -go verb. Podría. Of course it was podería, but many years of podería, podería, podería, podería, the e fell away, podría. How is to put?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Poner.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Poner. And I would put?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Pondría.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Pondría. Good. So there's a subtle difference in sound between I would be able to, podría, and I would put, pondría. We would be able to?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Pondríamos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: We would be able to. That's we would put.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Podríamos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Podríamos. And we would put?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Pondríamos.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Pondríamos.
